title: C1381E — Powertrain control module (PCM) connector
introduction:
The PCM uses sensor information to manage powertrain functions and command devices such as injectors and timing-control valves. I use this reference as its connector address book: the drawing locates a cavity, and the assignment table identifies the circuit listed there. The address tells you where a conversation travels; it does not prove everyone on the line is behaving.

Start with the connector identity and harness information. In the drawing, the broad left cavity bank and smaller right bank have separate rows. Find the printed cavity label, then read its complete table row across Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number. The functions distinguish sensor signals, control outputs, references, returns and fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies.

Keep repeated cavity entries separate: some list different gauge and terminal combinations without a qualifier that selects between them. Blank assignments and gray shading should be read alongside the table; shading has no supplied legend. Gauge conventions and the Size and Used codes are not defined here. This is an identification reference, with no physical viewing-direction confirmation, access instructions, probing method or electrical test limits. Use the applicable service or diagnostic procedure before working on the connection.

The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions in the supplied drawing. This discrepancy remains unresolved; the reference does not establish additional physical cavities or a corrected count.

edits.why: I match the harness identification before using the cavity drawing. The housing outline and projections help distinguish areas of the illustration, but they do not establish release functions or the physical viewing direction. Locate cavities by their printed labels rather than by estimating a position from the housing shape.

Read across the entire matching row to connect the cavity address with its circuit identity, wire description, function and terminal listing. A control output commands a device; a sensor signal reports a condition; references and returns have their own listed roles. Those distinctions explain the connection without establishing a test result or condemning the PCM. Repeated entries remain separate records, and a blank qualifier does not identify which applies to a particular vehicle.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata gives Pin Count as 98, while the supplied drawing labels cavities 1 through 95. The evidence does not reconcile that count with this view; confirm the intended count or drawing coverage before presenting them as consistent.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 118 primary units, six complete pages/one figure and two edits. Original first CLI author covered 54 units/two headings. Sole public addition discloses count disagreement. Original partial author remains separate; physical count and unqualified gauge/terminal alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
